description.narrative: The objective of the Financial Sector Support Project is to improve financial market infrastructure, regulatory and oversight capacity of Bangladesh Bank and access to long term financing for private firms in Bangladesh. There are four components to the project, the first component being strengthening financial market infrastructure. The component will build on previous efforts and improve financial market infrastructure further, specifically focusing on activities in the following four broad areas: (1) payment and settlement system development; (2) expanding and modernizing the Credit Information Bureau (CIB); (3) strengthening the systems of the Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) and integration with systems of other stakeholders; and (4) strengthening the information technology (IT) governance and IT management of the BB, optimizing the IT assets of the BB, and raising awareness of IT security aspects for the financial industry. The second component is the strengthening the financial sector regulator. This component aims to strengthen BB's capacity to regulate and supervise the scheduled financial institutions (banks and nonbank financial institutions), run the FIU more efficiently, and further develop and deepen the financial sector with new and innovative products. The third component is the supporting long term finance. This component will support long-term financing (an expected average of five years of financing) through PFIs to firms, particularly exporters, in Bangladesh. Finally, the fourth component is the project management and monitoring. Management of project implementation will be assumed by the Financial Sector Support Project (FSSP) cell in BB. The component will include costs for project management, monitoring and evaluation (M&E), capacity building and Governance and Accountability Action Plan (GAAP) implementation.

The project development objective is to improve financial market infrastructure, regulatory and oversight capacity of Bangladesh Bank and access to long term financing for private firms in Bangladesh.

title.narrative: Performance on BCP assessment: Number of principles on which Bangladesh Bank is judged as largely compliant and compliant.

comment.narrative:
<p>The result indicator was not achieved at the project closure. The target for this PDO indicator was revised downward from 12 to eight during the first project restructuring to reflect delays in implementation and an adjustment to a more realistic goal.</p>

<p>A comprehensive assessment of the Bangladeshi banking system against the Basel Core Principles (BCP) has been conducted jointly by the IMF and World Bank as part of the Financial Sector Assessment Program (FSAP) in March 2019. The FSAP assessment found Bangladesh Bank to be largely compliant with five BCP principles, which remained current at the project closure: </p>

<ul>
 <li>BCP 3: Cooperation and collaboration,</li>
 <li>BCP 4: Permissible activities,</li>
 <li>BCP 7: Major acquisitions,</li>
 <li>BCP 22: Market risk and</li>
 <li>BCP 24: Liquidity risk.</li>
</ul>

<p>Additionally, in the follow-up communications with the Bangladesh Bank, the FSAP team revised the assessment from Materially Non-Compliant (MNC) to Largely Compliant (LC) grades for two more BCPs:</p>

<ul>
 <li>BCP 10: Supervisory reporting and</li>
 <li>BCP 13: Home-host relationships.</li>
</ul>

<p>During the mission, the ICR team has found that Bangladesh Bank has achieved major progress towards achieving compliance with four more BCPs. Under FSSP, Bangladesh Bank hired a bank supervision consultant firm (AFC Germany) who worked with the BankingRegulations and Policy Department (BRPD), Banking Inspection Departments (DBIs), and Department of Off-site Supervision (DOS). AFC Germany identified 6(six) additional BCPs, where significant progress was achieved, and they can be assessed next for compliance:???????</p>

<ul>
 <li>BCP 05: Licensing Criteria</li>
 <li>BCP 21: Country and Transfer Risks</li>
 <li>BCP 23: Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book</li>
 <li>BCP 28: Disclosure and Transparency</li>
 <li>BCP 14: Corporate Governance</li>
 <li>BCP 26: Internal Control and Audit???????</li>
</ul>

<p>However, assessment of compliance with these additional BCPs can be done only in the formal FSAP process. </p>

title.narrative: NPLs in project-funded in foreign-denominated long-term finance portfolio

comment.narrative: <p>Archived. This indicator obviously was designed as a cap of 7% NPL, not as a target, meaning the less NPL the project portfolio has the better its implied performance. In this way, the project exceeded the target by not reaching the maximum level of 7% (in fact out of 56 financed subprojects, none has overdue payments; all the subprojects are still classified as standard/performing).  </p>
<p>Achieved. The project exceeded the original target for this indicator in the first year of implementation. </p>

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The indicator exceeded the end-target value in the first year of implementation of the project. </p>

title.narrative: Cumulative number of Bangladesh Bank banking supervision officers trained on risk-based supervision

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The indicator was revised during the July 2019 restructuring downwards from 500 to 300 based on the reason that it was over-estimated, not reflecting the smaller number of actual supervision officers that would benefit from risk-based supervision training. The revised indicator was exceeded at the project closure. </p>

title.narrative: Cumulative number of participants and trainees at Training Of Trainers (TOT) and other workshops delivered to industry on safeguards and health and safety

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The target indicator was streamlined during July 2019 restructuring to exclude awareness campaigns, which was too broad and hard to quantify and focus instead on the cumulative number of participants at the training. The target value was revised down from 64 to 50 accordingly. The project exceeded the declared end-target in the fourth year of implementation. </p>

<p>Achieved. The target has been revised downward from 250 to 55 during the first project restructuring in June 2019 quoting the reason that it was initially over-estimated, not reflecting the nature of demand or constraints from WB safeguards. The project achieved the revised target at the closure date with 56 cases disbursed, two more approved for disbursement, and one more in the pipeline. </p>

Percentage of Government Payments by value processed through electronic means (annually)

comment.narrative: <p>The result indicator was Achieved. The result indicator exceeded the target after the first year of project implementation when it reached 94.9% in 2016. The most recently reported percentage of government payments through electronic was 98.33% in end-December 2020. The next total government payment figure will not be available before the end of 2021.  </p>

comment.narrative: <p>The result indicator was achieved. The indicator has exceeded the end-target value after the second year of project implementation, when the outstanding FX Long term loans of Participating Financial Institutions reached US$ 627 million in June 2017.   </p>
